title: A Case for Competition in Information Provision
abstract: arXiv:2608.24129v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study how competition among biased news sources affects information and welfare when sources can misrepresent facts at a cost. Monopolistic and competitive market structures admit many equilibria. We develop a common belief-based selection criterion that applies to both and makes welfare comparisons possible. Under the refined outcomes, adding an oppositely biased source improves the receiver's welfare when that source faces sufficiently high misreporting costs. Competition disciplines the incumbent while introducing a few distortions of its own. Better information need not increase total welfare, and distorted advice from a monopolist can raise total welfare. Competition may improve decision-making without being socially beneficial.

translated_title: 信息供给中的竞争案例
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.24129v1 公告类型：新 摘要：我们研究了当新闻来源可以以一定成本歪曲事实时，有偏见的新闻来源之间的竞争如何影响信息和福利。垄断和竞争市场结构存在许多均衡。我们开发了一种基于共同信念的选择标准，适用于这两种结构，使福利比较成为可能。在精细化结果下，当对立偏见的来源面临足够高的虚假报告成本时，添加该来源会改善接收者的福利。竞争约束了现有来源，同时引入了自身的一些扭曲。更好的信息不一定增加总福利，垄断者的扭曲建议可能提高总福利。竞争可能改善决策但不一定对社会有益。
tldr: 本文通过共同信念选择标准分析偏见新闻来源的竞争，发现竞争在特定成本条件下能改善决策但未必提升总福利，垄断扭曲建议反而可能增加福利。
en_tdlr: This paper analyzes competition among biased news sources using a common belief-based selection criterion, finding that competition can improve decision-making under certain cost conditions but may not enhance total welfare, while monopolistic distorted advice could raise welfare.
